item.title: Cell-free protein synthesis for next-generation biomanufacturing.
item.abstract: Chemicals with diverse molecular structures are essential to the pharmaceutical, food, and specialty chemical industries; however, their sustainable production remains challenging due to complex cellular regulation, limited metabolic flexibility, and the scalability constraints of purified enzyme-based systems. Extract-based cell-free protein synthesis (CFPS) has emerged as a versatile biomanufacturing platform that enables the production of functional enzymes in vitro and provides an open, programmable environment for constructing synthetic biosynthetic systems beyond the constraints of living cells. By decoupling chemical synthesis from cellular growth, CFPS allows precise control over enzyme composition, pathway stoichiometry, and cofactor utilization, thereby improving catalytic efficiency and resource utilization. In this review, we summarize recent advances in extract-based CFPS for chemical biosynthesis and discuss key engineering strategies, including cofactor regeneration, pathway balancing, and semicontinuous operation, to enhance system performance. Furthermore, we highlight emerging opportunities to integrate CFPS with artificial intelligence-guided design, renewable feedstocks, and modular reactor technologies toward more sustainable and scalable biomanufacturing processes.

item.title: Base editing-mediated precision genome engineering in Toxoplasma gondii.
item.abstract: Functional genomics in Toxoplasma gondii (T. gondii), an obligate intracellular parasite of global medical importance, primarily relies on CRISPR-Cas9-mediated gene disruption. However, conventional CRISPR-Cas9 editing relies on generating double-strand breaks (DSBs), which are repaired either by error-prone non-homologous end joining or by homology-directed repair requiring donor templates and time-consuming clone isolation. Here, we established the first two base editor platforms in T. gondii: adenine base editors (ABEs) and cytosine base editors (CBEs), which enable precise point mutations via direct base conversion without DSBs or donor templates. We successfully employed ABE and CBE to introduce high-efficiency A > G and C > T conversions at defined genomic loci, respectively. By targeting the critical virulence gene ROP18, we demonstrate that ABE-mediated i-Silence (start codon disruption) and CBE-mediated i-STOP (premature stop codon introduction) strategies can efficiently generate functional T. gondii null mutants. The resulting base-edited parasite strains exhibited a complete loss of ROP18 protein expression and showed attenuated virulence and proliferation phenotypes equivalent to those of a conventional ROP18 knockout strain, as validated in both cellular and mouse models. We then conducted a genome-wide analysis predicting that the i-Silence and i-STOP strategies enable targeted inactivation of nearly all genes in the T. gondii genome (>99.6% coverage). Since our approach does not require DSBs, it enables researchers to achieve efficient, precise nucleotide substitutions without the risk of chromosomal rearrangements. We propose base editing as a powerful genetic tool in T. gondii, paving the way for high-resolution functional pathogenesis studies and the further development of genetically stable attenuated vaccines.

item.title: Chromosome-scale CRISPR screening reveals secretory pathway genes as drivers of aneuploidy-mediated antifungal tolerance
item.abstract: The gain or loss of chromosomes in eukaryotes often drives aberrant phenotypes by altering the expression levels of hundreds or thousands of genes. In the case of beneficial aneuploidies, the genetic basis of fitness improvement has rarely been pinpointed, and identifying the causal genes remains a major challenge in engineering biology. The leading cause of human fungal infections, Candida albicans, frequently acquires extra copies of chromosome R (ChrR) following exposure to azole antifungal drugs, resulting in heightened antifungal tolerance. Despite this, why this aneuploidy frequently emerges following azole exposure and how it promotes antifungal tolerance remain unknown. Here, we combine RNA-seq with parallel chromosome-wide CRISPR activation (CRISPRa) and CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screens to systematically profile the ChrR genes contributing to azole tolerance. Using multiplexed CRISPR-dCas12a tools, we further characterize the combinatorial effects of candidate genes and uncover a central role for post-Golgi secretory trafficking in antifungal tolerance. Specifically, we demonstrate that the secretory pathway regulators SEC4 and YPT31 are both necessary and sufficient for ChrR-mediated azole tolerance, and drive increased ergosterol content in the cell membrane. By leveraging a large-scale CRISPRa screen in a fungal pathogen, our work functionally dissects one of the most common aneuploidies observed in C. albicans, provides mechanistic insight into the molecular basis of antifungal tolerance, and establishes a generalizable framework for studying aneuploidy-mediated phenotypes across eukaryotic organisms.

item.title: A Synthetic Benchmark for Topology-Aware Modeling of Multispecific Antibody Function.
item.abstract: Multispecific antibodies (msAbs) offer transformative therapeutic potential by engaging multiple epitopes simultaneously, yet their efficacy is an emergent property governed by complex molecular architectures. Rational design is often bottlenecked by the inability to predict how subtle changes in domain topology influence functional outcomes, a challenge exacerbated by the scarcity of comprehensive experimental data. Here, we introduce Synapse, a biologically inspired synthetic benchmark for topology-aware modeling of msAbs. First, we present a generative method that combines nonlinear per-domain sequence-to-score landscapes with connectivity-dependent synthetic readouts. Second, we propose a graph neural network architecture that explicitly encodes these topological constraints, distinguishing between format configurations that appear identical to the evaluated connectivity-agnostic multilayer perceptron. We demonstrate that this model learns topology-dependent structure-function relationships on synthetic landscapes and evaluate a transfer learning workflow as infrastructure for adaptation to biological datasets. We showcase our framework with a trispecific T cell engager-inspired synthetic topology-dependent optimization task and a constrained ranking of common light chain candidates against a composite objective. This work provides a controlled benchmarking environment for developing and evaluating topology-aware computational tools for msAb modeling. All experiments use synthetic data; no biological validation is performed.

item.title: Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase bifunctionally catalyzes ring formation involving sequential terminal carbon oxidation for pyrrolizidinone alkaloid biosynthesis.
item.abstract: The Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenase UcsF plays a key role in the early biosynthesis of UCS1025A, an antibacterial and antitumor pyrrolizidinone alkaloid, by participating in the formation of its core ring scaffold. UcsF catalyzes sequential oxidation of the terminal C5 of L-isoleucine, ultimately generating a five-membered ring product, (2S,3S)-3,4-dihydro-3-methyl-2H-pyrrole-2-carboxylic acid. This catalytic process is vital in the construction of natural product skeletons and synthetic biology. However, the molecular basis of UcsF and its unique two-step catalytic mechanism remain poorly understood. We characterized the catalytic function of UcsF, determined its crystal structure and combined molecular docking and MD simulations to reveal the molecular basis for substrate recognition, and employed quantum chemical calculations on reaction-state models to investigate plausible reaction pathways underlying the sequential oxidation. UcsF exhibits catalytic activity toward 2-amino carboxylic acid substrates. The crystal structure of UcsF features a unique open active pocket, with substrate binding defined by the collective contributions of multiple structural modules. In the catalytic reaction, the Fe(IV) = O species abstracts a hydrogen atom from the C5 position of L-isoleucine, followed by hydroxyl rebound to complete the first hydroxylation step. Combined kinetic, solvent isotope-effect, mutational, and computational analyses support a preferred Asp279'-facilitated PCET pathway for the second oxidation of 5-OH-Ile to the aldehyde product. Our study provides a molecular basis for understanding the relationship between the structure and function of Fe(II)/2-oxoglutarate-dependent dioxygenases and reveals the potential of the catalytic ability of UcsF for biosynthesis.

item.title: Altitudin S, an Antimicrobial Peptide Produced by Bacillus altitudinis ECC22, Defines a Novel Subgroup of Circular Bacteriocins.
item.abstract: Bacteriocins are ribosomally synthesized antimicrobial peptides with diverse structures and mechanisms of action. Bacillus altitudinis ECC22, previously shown to produce the circular bacteriocins pumilarin and altitudin A, was found to harbor an additional biosynthetic gene cluster (BGC) encoding a novel circular bacteriocin, designated altitudin S. Proteomic analysis of purified active supernatant fractions confirmed the production of altitudin S, with a molecular mass of 8379.7 Da, while LC-MS/MS identification of a peptide spanning the N-to-C-terminal junction provided direct evidence of head-to-tail cyclization. Altitudin S is synthesized as a 132-residue precursor comprising a 56-amino-acid leader and a 76-residue circular mature core. Structural modeling predicted a compact saposin-like fold composed of five α-helices and a strongly cationic surface (pI ≈ 11.0, net charge + 13). Altitudin S was also produced using an in vitro cell-free protein synthesis system coupled with split-intein mediated ligation (IV-CFPS/SIML) and exhibited a narrow antimicrobial spectrum. Comprehensive sequence and phylogenetic analyses revealed that altitudin S is a highly divergent circular bacteriocin with distinctive sequence features and predicted physicochemical properties, including an exceptionally high isoelectric point, strong cationic charge, and low hydrophobicity. Homologs were identified across diverse Bacillales species, displaying high sequence similarity, conserved structural features, and a shared predicted physicochemical profile. Their BGCs were also highly conserved and consistently encoded an M48-family metallopeptidase. Collectively, these findings support the proposal of altitudin S and its homologs as representatives of a novel third subgroup (subgroup III) of circular bacteriocins.

item.title: FANIN/Zfp148, the upstream regulator of pioneer factor paralogs Foxa1 and Foxa2, controls hepatocyte identity.
item.abstract: Numerous attempts involving combinations of transcription factors to create functional hepatocytes to enable implantation into patients with chronic and end-stage liver disease have been promising but not yet successful. We identified the upstream regulator of pioneer factor paralogs Foxa1 and Foxa2 in Mus Musculus, critical to hepatogenesis and adult physiological function, we named FANIN. Winged-helix (forkhead) factor paralogs Foxa1 and Foxa2, originally named HNF3α and HNF3β, are called pioneer factors for their ability to independently bind closed chromatin and change chromatin accessibility allowing other factors to bind. Foxa1 and Foxa2, unlike a close homolog Foxa3, are required for life. Deletion of FANIN, encoded by Zfp148, leads to loss of Foxa1 and Foxa2 expression in the liver. FANIN affects global changes in chromatin accessibility, not observed in Foxa2 or Foxa1/Foxa2 double mutants, in particular at regions with enriched HNF4α motif. FANIN controls hepatocyte identity through regulating Foxa1 & Foxa2 expression, as well as activity/binding of HNF4α. Hence, FANIN modulates master regulators that control hepatocyte-specific gene expression and identity. In particular, reduced synergistic Foxa2/HNF4α function in FANIN mutants leads to destabilization of the hepatocyte, resulting in hepatic vacuolization, proliferation, and severe injury. We have uncovered a novel genetic circuit involving master regulators of the hepatocyte, which has significant implications for regeneration of these cells in patients with severe liver disease.

item.title: Environmental Microbiomes as Sources of Postbiotic Therapeutics: A One Health Perspective on Translational Applications.
item.abstract: Environmental microbiomes are reservoirs of specialized microorganisms with implications for ecosystem functionality, host health, and therapeutic discovery. Soil, marine, plant-associated, wastewater, freshwater, and extreme-environment microbiomes contain communities capable of producing bioactive metabolites and functional biomolecules. Postbiotics-non-viable microorganisms and their functional components that confer health benefits-offer potential advantages in stability, safety, scalability, and pharmaceutical development. This review examines environmental microbiomes as sources of postbiotic therapeutics within a One Health framework. A critical integrative translational review synthesized literature on environmental microbiomes, postbiotic diversity, molecular mechanisms, therapeutic applications, technological advances, and barriers to clinical translation. Evidence was organized across ecological sources, postbiotic classes, human-health applications, discovery platforms, pharmaceutical development, and translational challenges. Environmental microbiomes represent chemically and functionally diverse reservoirs of postbiotic candidates shaped by ecological adaptation, microbial competition, and environmental selection. Major classes-including short-chain fatty acids, bacteriocins, extracellular vesicles, indole and tryptophan metabolites, exopolysaccharides, and microbial/lytic enzymes-act through receptor signaling, immune modulation, barrier protection, antimicrobial activity, metabolic regulation, intercellular communication, and enzymatic target modification. Metagenomics, metabolomics, artificial intelligence, synthetic biology, organoid and microfluidic models, advanced delivery systems, and biomanufacturing increasingly enable discovery and development. However, reproducibility, microbiome variability, manufacturing scalability, regulatory standardization, cost, and equitable translation remain barriers. Environmental microbiomes provide important reservoirs for postbiotic discovery. Integrating ecological microbiology with multi-omics, computational innovation, pharmaceutical engineering, and human-relevant validation could accelerate development of defined, reproducible, and scalable postbiotic therapeutics. Preserving microbial ecosystem diversity is relevant to environmental sustainability and future microbiome-derived therapeutic innovation within One Health medicine.

item.title: Minimal functional activity and presence of an antigen sink limit CD36 blockade as a macrophage-targeted cancer immunotherapy.
item.abstract: Targeting macrophages in the tumor microenvironment offers potential to relieve immune-suppression and improve anti-tumor immune responses. Unfortunately, a range of tumor-associated macrophage (TAM)-targeting agents in development has not yet translated into clinical benefit. We sought to identify novel targets on primary human macrophages through an unbiased phenotypic selection campaign. This work identified the scavenger receptor and lipid transporter CD36 as a potential target associated with anti-inflammatory phenotypes on macrophages. We first confirmed the ability of in-house generated and commercially available anti-CD36 monoclonal antibodies (mAbs) to inhibit CD36 binding and cellular uptake of oxidized lipids, both in cell-free settings and in engineered cell lines. However, we were unable to observe consistent or robust responses to CD36 blockade in primary human macrophages using a range of TAM-like and lipid-induced in vitro models. In vivo, CD36-KO mice showed reduced tumor growth, which implicated a CD36-dependent host impact on tumor progression. Importantly, anti-CD36 mAb failed to phenocopy this effect. Pharmacokinetic assessments revealed considerable target-mediated drug disposition with anti-CD36 mAb, limiting free plasma concentrations of the drug. A modified dosing regimen managed to increase drug concentration in plasma but still failed to elicit meaningful activity across primary tumor models, with/without anti-PD-L1. Although it remains clear that lipid uptake and metabolism is a key feature in TAM that can drive their immunosuppressive activities, our investigation raises concerns regarding the therapeutic targeting of CD36 due to redundancy in the lipid scavenging receptor family and a broad tissue expression profile. Together, these findings suggest that conventional monoclonal antibody blockade of CD36 has limited therapeutic potential in solid tumors, although outcomes may vary in different biological contexts.

item.title: A TMEM175 Mutation Disrupts the Lysosomal-Mitochondrial Axis Causing Short QT Syndrome and Sudden Cardiac Death
item.abstract: Short QT Syndrome (SQTS) is a rare cardiac channelopathy characterized by abnormally short QTc intervals and increased sudden cardiac death (SCD) risk. Only 20-30% of SQTS cases have been linked to genetic mutations, typi-cally in surface membrane ion channels. We identified a novel lysosomal TMEM175 gene mutation (p.Arg377His) in 7 patients in a family with SQTS and SCD. Genetic analyses, including whole exome sequencing in the family and rare-variant burden testing in [~]118,000 UK Biobank participants, sug-gested an association between TMEM175 rare variants and QT interval short-ening. Functional studies in CRISPR-engineered mice and patient-specific induced pluripotent stem cell-derived cardiomyocytes (iPSC-CMs) revealed that TMEM175R377H causes shortened QT intervals and hastened repolariza-tion, respectively, as well an increased arrhythmia susceptibility. Isolated TMEM175R377H cardiomyocytes showed action potential duration (APD) abbre-viation, confirmed in whole TMEM175R377H mouse hearts and patient-specific iPSC-CM monolayers. In silico and electron microscopy studies showed that TMEM175R377H disrupts lysosomal-mitochondrial interactions, leading to mito-chondrial dysfunction, as evidenced by the reduced maximal respiration and spare respiratory capacity, with reduced ATP production, IKATP activation, and APD shortening. This mutation represents the first non-sarcolemmal ion chan-nel defect associated with SQTS and high SCD risk, potentially expanding the genetic landscape of the disease.

item.title: Recent approaches to modulate citrinin biosynthesis in Monascus species: a review.
item.abstract: The filamentous fungi Monascus spp. are rich sources of secondary metabolites that include Monascus azaphilone pigments, monacolin K, and γ-aminobutyric acid, making them significant in the food, nutraceutical, cosmetic and pharmaceutical industries. Despite the industrial importance of this fungus, its production of citrinin, a nephrotoxic polyketide mycotoxin, remains a major drawback and limits its commercial application. Recent research studies have shown that the mechanism that governs citrinin biosynthesis highlights the interactions between Biosynthetic Gene Clusters (BGCs), epigenetic modifications, global regulatory networks, and environmental factors. The current understanding of the molecular and epigenetic mechanisms used to mitigate citrinin production in Monascus spp. is discussed in this review. Emphasis is given on histone acetylation and deacetylation, methylation, chromatin remodeling, the velvet complex, and the modulation of toxin biosynthesis through RNA-level gene expression control. The recent advances are critically evaluated for engineering citrinin-free strains, including transcriptomics, proteomics, multi-omics, RNA interference, CRISPR/Cas genome editing, and synthetic biology. The comparative analysis of these approaches shows that integrating epigenetic engineering with advanced genome and metabolic engineering can regulate citrinin while maintaining other important metabolite yields. Combining multi-omics and artificial intelligence-guided strain design with epigenetic interventions will accelerate the development of safe, sustainable, and high-yielding Monascus-assisted bioprocesses.

item.title: Molecular characterization of tetracycline resistance mechanisms in the probiotic strain Lentilactobacillus buchneri KU200793.
item.abstract:
UNLABELLED: Tetracycline resistance in probiotic lactic acid bacteria raises safety concerns for food applications. This study investigated the mechanisms underlying tetracycline resistance in Lentilactobacillus buchneri KU200793 using genomic, biochemical, and functional analyses. The tetracycline minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) was 128 mg/L, exceeding the European Food Safety Authority cut-off. Genome annotation identified putative resistance-associated genes, including major facilitator superfamily and ATP-binding cassette transporters, PmrA, and a TetR family transcriptional regulator. HPLC analysis indicated that extracellular components from tetracycline-exposed cultures may affect tetracycline stability, but not through direct inactivation. No mutations were detected in the 30S ribosomal protein S10 or 16S rRNA compared to susceptible L. buchneri ATCC 4005. Notably, chlorpromazine reduced the MIC 16-fold, to 8 mg/L, identifying chlorpromazine-sensitive efflux as the major resistance determinant. Reduced alkaline phosphatase activity and partial restoration of cell-free green fluorescent protein translation provided supportive evidence for decreased permeability and inducible translation-associated factors in this multifactorial phenotype.
SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s10068-026-02296-5.

item.title: Formulation-controlled redaporfin cellular-targeted photodynamic therapy sensitizes tumors to PD-1/PD-L1 blockade via immunogenic cell death.
item.abstract: Redaporfin is a clinically advanced photosensitizer developed for vascular-targeted photodynamic therapy (V-PDT), yet its therapeutic utility under long drug-to-light interval, cellular-targeted PDT (C-PDT), remains limited despite substantial tumor exposure. Here, we show that formulation-dependent control of redaporfin photochemistry and ER-associated intracellular localization can convert otherwise non-curative C-PDT into an effective partner for immune checkpoint blockade. Encapsulation in Pluronic®-based micelles prolonged the redaporfin triplet-state lifetime over sevenfold relative to ethanol and over twentyfold relative to a non-micellar aqueous environment, while preserving oxygen accessibility. Direct comparison with Pluronic® F127 demonstrated carrier-specific effects: despite greater cell-free ROS generation, F127 showed lower encapsulation efficiency, poorer storage stability, and inferior intracellular ROS generation and phototoxicity. P123 enhanced ER-associated redaporfin accumulation at 24 h and amplified an ICD phenotype, evidenced by increased calreticulin exposure and HMGB1 release; P123-mediated C-PDT also activated macrophages with an M1-like marker profile and induced adaptive PD-L1 upregulation in surviving CT26 cells. In vivo fluorescence imaging confirmed rapid tumor accumulation and sustained retention of redaporfin/P123 at 24 h. Whereas C-PDT alone and α-PD-L1 monotherapy were non-curative, combination with PD-1 and/or PD-L1 blockade produced durable complete responses in up to 50% of mice. All complete responders remained tumor-free during 120-day follow-up, and dual blockade conferred protection against CT26 rechallenge, providing functional evidence of long-term antitumor immune memory. These findings establish formulation-driven control of intracellular photochemistry and subcellular localization as an underappreciated determinant of PDT-mediated anticancer immunity and provide a translational strategy for repurposing a clinically advanced V-PDT photosensitizer for durable photodynamic immunotherapy.

item.title: Lactiplantibacillus plantarum postbiotics attenuate Salmonella LPS-triggered neuroinflammation by modulating the microbiota-gut-brain axis in a pig model.
item.abstract: This study explored the effects of Lactiplantibacillus plantarum (LP) postbiotics on Salmonella LPS-induced neuroinflammation, and elucidated the underlying mechanisms. Sixty pigs were randomly divided into control, lipopolysaccharide (LPS), cell-free supernatant of LP (CFS) and CFS + LPS groups. The pigs were fed with 0.8% CFS or MRS medium for 28 days, and then exposed to 30 μg kg-1 LPS. The results showed that CFS alleviated damage of the liver, colon and brain, and improved brain tight junctions. LPS significantly upregulated the levels of IL-1β, IL-6 and TNF-α (P < 0.05) and downregulated IL-4 and IL-10 (P < 0.05), while CFS pretreatment markedly reversed this trend. LPS activated the brain inflammasome by increasing NLRP3, IL-1β, IL-18 and GSDMD (P < 0.05), and CFS pretreatment significantly decreased NLRP3 and IL-1β (P < 0.05). CFS modulated the levels of neurotransmitters, particularly the tryptophan metabolism. Moreover, CFS markedly increased the contents of microbial metabolites (P < 0.05) and optimized the gut microbiota through improving Lactobacillus amylovorus and Lactobacillus reuteri (P < 0.05). To further clarify the role of the microbiota on alleviating neuroinflammation, the fecal microbial transplantation (FMT) model in mice was established. The mice were administered with fecal suspension from CFS-treated pigs for 14 days and challenged with 3 × 108 CFU Salmonella Typhimurium (ST) for three days. The results showed that the weight loss caused by ST was significantly alleviated by CFS and FMT-CFS pretreatment (P < 0.05). FMT-CFS markedly inhibited ST translocation in the spleen and brain (P < 0.05), and attenuated tissue damage. FMT-CFS dramatically suppressed neuroinflammation and NLRP3 activation. In summary, LP postbiotics attenuated Salmonella LPS-induced neuroinflammation via modulating the microbiota-gut-brain axis. Our findings provide the potential of postbiotics as a nutritional supplement to alleviate neuroinflammation.

item.title: Plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA sequencing identifies clinically unsuspected cases of Toxoplasma gondii infection in immunocompromised patients: a single-centre experience.
item.abstract: Toxoplasmosis can be challenging to diagnose, particularly in immunocompromised patients with nonspecific clinical presentations. We present a retrospective, single-centre case series of eight Toxoplasma gondii infections identified by plasma metagenomic cell-free DNA (cfDNA) sequencing in allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplant recipients. Nested within a larger cohort evaluating cfDNA utilization, this case series highlights a positive clinical impact of cfDNA testing in 5 out of 8 (62.5%) patients, including earlier diagnosis and changes in clinical management. These findings illustrate the potential utility of plasma cfDNA sequencing as a complement to conventional diagnostics across diverse clinical presentations of toxoplasmosis.

cards.title_cn: 广东深圳：以"数据穿透+行刑联动+事前拦截"全链条整治超量开药
cards.one_liner: 深圳医保部门针对门诊共济改革后的超量开药骗保行为，建立事前拦截与行刑联动机制。
key_findings: 联合公安抓获犯罪嫌疑人30名，涉案金额200余万元，15人被依法处理。
开发11类超量开药事前提醒规则，累计预警超16万次，拦截金额超3600万元。
构建知识图谱精准画像，行刑联动全链条打击职业骗保。
cards.why_it_matters: 医保基金监管趋严，涉及处方与用药数据的合规要求提高；合成生物学企业若涉及诊断、用药或医保支付相关产品，需关注数据穿透与事前拦截规则对处方行为的影响。

cards.score_reason: 长护险宣传，与研究方向弱相关
cards.title_cn: 长护送暖入家门 温情守护夕阳红
cards.one_liner: 国家医保局发布沈阳长期护理保险制度落地案例，展示居家护理服务实效。
key_findings: 长期护理师定期上门，为卧床老人提供擦浴、压疮护理等服务
褥疮逐步愈合，留置尿管风险得到有效控制
该案例体现辽宁省沈阳市长护险制度从纸面落到地面
cards.why_it_matters: 长护险属医保支付政策，与合成生物学研发方向关联较弱；但若关注老年护理、医疗器械或居家检测产品准入，可留意医保支付导向。

cards.title_cn: 2026年10月金融统计数据报告
cards.one_liner: 央行发布10月金融数据：社融存量同比增7.2%，实体经济人民币贷款余额279.31万亿元。
key_findings: 10月末社融存量同比增7.2%，对实体经济发放的人民币贷款余额279.31万亿元。
对实体经济人民币贷款占同期社融存量59.5%，外币贷款折人民币余额1.26万亿元。
前十个月人民币存款增加21.97万亿元，10月末存款余额350.65万亿元。
cards.why_it_matters: 这是宏观金融总量数据，与合成生物学研发、产业融资无直接监管关联；可作判断生物医药信贷与资本环境的背景参考。

item.title: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet
item.abstract: Introducing ChatGPT Wallet, a secure way for agents in ChatGPT Work, Codex, and dots to complete purchases with user approval and existing card protections.

cards.score_reason: ChatGPT支付能力重大产品发布
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 推出 ChatGPT Wallet：让 AI 代理代用户完成支付
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 发布 ChatGPT Wallet，ChatGPT Work、Codex 与 dots 中的代理可在用户批准下完成购买。
key_findings: 代理在 ChatGPT Work、Codex、dots 中发起购买，须经用户批准后执行。
沿用现有银行卡保护机制，强调支付安全与用户可控。
面向工作流场景，把支付能力嵌入 AI 代理执行链路。
cards.why_it_matters: AI 代理从信息处理延伸到实际交易执行，合成生物学研发中的试剂采购、云服务与外包订单或可自动化，需关注支付授权与合规边界。

item.title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
item.abstract: Researcher traces a path from AI reward hacking to potential human extinction.

cards.score_reason: OpenAI董事AI风险言论值得关注
cards.title_cn: OpenAI 董事警告：AI 接管社会可能仅剩数月
cards.one_liner: OpenAI 董事援引奖励黑客研究，警告 AI 接管社会或仅剩数月。
key_findings: 研究者将 AI 奖励黑客行为与人类灭绝风险联系起来
OpenAI 董事会成员公开表达对 AI 接管社会时间表的担忧
警告称从奖励黑客到潜在人类灭绝存在演化路径
cards.why_it_matters: 合成生物学依赖 AI 设计蛋白与基因线路，奖励黑客风险直接关系实验安全与生物安全治理，值得关注 AI 安全讨论对科研工具的影响。

item.title: How Amplitude ships product improvements in 1–2 days with OpenAI
item.abstract: Built primarily on OpenAI models, Amplitude’s proactive product agent, Wave, identifies what to build, helps teams ship changes with coding agents, and measures the impact.

cards.score_reason: OpenAI企业应用案例常规
cards.title_cn: Amplitude 借助 OpenAI 模型实现 1–2 天交付产品改进
cards.one_liner: Amplitude 基于 OpenAI 模型构建产品智能体 Wave，将产品改进交付周期缩短至 1–2 天。
key_findings: Wave 以 OpenAI 模型为核心，自动识别应开发的产品功能。
该智能体协助团队借助编码智能体完成改动并交付。
交付后由 Wave 度量改动带来的实际影响。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学研发而言，可借鉴“识别—构建—度量”闭环智能体模式，加速菌株或元件的设计-构建-测试-学习迭代。

item.title: Opening the datasets behind our AI weather models
item.abstract: Foundational precipitation and geostationary satellite datasets to observe the planet clearly.

cards.score_reason: 气象数据集与关注领域弱相关
cards.title_cn: DeepMind 开放 AI 气象模型数据集
cards.one_liner: DeepMind 公开其 AI 气象模型所用的降水与地球静止卫星基础数据集。
key_findings: 开放降水与地球静止卫星两类基础数据集，用于清晰观测地球。
数据来自 Google DeepMind Blog，面向 AI 气象模型研发。
cards.why_it_matters: 高质量气象数据集可支撑 AI 模型训练与验证；对合成生物学读者而言，或可辅助环境与气候相关研究的数据获取。

item.title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
item.abstract: Airlines praised the AI tool, but the air traffic controllers’ union wasn’t involved.

cards.score_reason: 空管AI与关注领域弱相关
cards.title_cn: FAA将AI建议工具扩展至全美空域，用于管理空中交通拥堵
cards.one_liner: FAA把AI拥堵管理建议工具从局部试点扩展至全美空域，但空管工会未参与。
key_findings: FAA将AI建议工具覆盖范围扩大至全美空域，用于管理空中交通拥堵
航空公司对该AI工具表示赞赏
空管工会未被纳入该工具的推进过程
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学无直接关联，但可作为AI在高风险监管场景落地的案例，供关注AI治理与合规的读者参考。

item.title: How AI Is Helping Care Teams Get Patients the Right Care, Sooner
item.abstract: From pediatric research to smart hospitals, AI is helping care teams spend less time on routine tasks and more time with patients. Health systems and startups are putting it to work across healthcare, from matching patients to clinical trials to supporting radiologists, hospital teams and patients at home. Clinicians stay at the center, reviewing AI […]

cards.score_reason: 医疗AI应用弱相关
cards.title_cn: AI 助力医疗团队让患者更早获得合适诊疗
cards.one_liner: NVIDIA 报道 AI 在儿科研究、智慧医院等场景中减少常规事务，让医护有更多时间照护患者。
key_findings: AI 用于患者与临床试验匹配、辅助放射科医生及居家患者支持。
医院与初创公司在儿科研究到智慧医院等多场景落地 AI 工具。
临床医生始终居中，负责审核 AI 输出并保留最终决策权。
cards.why_it_matters: 对合成生物学背景读者，AI 辅助临床试验匹配与医院流程优化，可借鉴到基因治疗、诊断产品的临床转化与患者招募路径。

item.title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
item.abstract: "SignDrop" exploit lets local users gain all-powerful System rights.

cards.score_reason: Windows漏洞与关注领域无关
cards.title_cn: 不满研究者公开 Windows 0-day，攻击者可借此获取 System 权限
cards.one_liner: 研究者公开 Windows 0-day 漏洞「SignDrop」，本地用户可提权至 System。
key_findings: 「SignDrop」为本地提权漏洞，利用后可获得最高 System 权限
漏洞由不满的研究者公开披露，属 0-day，暂无官方补丁
攻击者需先具备本地访问权限，再借该漏洞完成提权
cards.why_it_matters: 实验室工作站与自动化设备多为 Windows，本地提权可危及菌株设计、序列与实验数据；建议核查补丁与访问控制。

item.title: Screenless GPS: Slate Auto says, "Remember the road atlas"
item.abstract: What’s more fitting than a spiral-bound map for a bare-bones two-door pickup?

cards.score_reason: 无屏GPS与自动驾驶弱相关
cards.title_cn: 无屏GPS：Slate Auto 呼吁“重拾公路地图册”
cards.one_liner: Slate Auto 为极简双门皮卡提出无屏GPS方案，主张回归纸质公路地图册。
key_findings: Slate Auto 的极简双门皮卡不配屏幕，导航改用螺旋装订的纸质地图册。
该方案以低成本、低复杂度替代车载屏幕导航。
报道来自 Ars Technica，属汽车产品设计新闻。
cards.why_it_matters: 与合成生物学无直接关联，但可作为极简产品设计与低成本硬件思路的参考，对实验室设备或便携检测装置的去屏幕化设计有启发。
